terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a leathern sack filled with sand, flour, etc., by means of which the athletae exercised in the palaestra”; in Cicero only figuratively.

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 3.4.16: ego tē follem pugillātōrium faciam, et pendentem incursābō pugnīs (Lewis & Short s.v. follis)
terms.comment: Plautus’s word for a ball struck with the fist, and his joke is a punching bag: “I’ll make a fist-ball of you and lay into you as you hang there.” Lewis & Short spells the adjective pugillātōrius or pugilātōrius.

sources: Lewis & Short: corycus · Lewis & Short: follis
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 46.
